quest.title: Mysterious Urban Legend
quest.description: You planned to visit the Yae Publishing House, but after arriving in Hanamizaka, you find that it is more lively than usual here...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x425, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We haven't been to the Yae Publishing House in a while. Paimon wonders if they have any new books in? The one we read with Ei that time was pretty cool...

dialogues.speaker: Takatoshi
dialogues.text: Come on, this is a no-brainer, man! There's only one thing worth wishing for — and that is a ton of Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Kiyoto
dialogues.text: But the exam's next week... If I fail again, I'm seriously done for. I'm better off wishing that my exam goes smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Takatoshi
dialogues.text: Ahh, it's just an exam! Trust me, there's no problem you can't solve by throwing Mora at it. If it doesn't work, then just keep throwing till it does!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are they arguing about? It's quite a spirited debate.

dialogues.speaker: Takatoshi
dialogues.text: Huh...? Really? You guys don't know?

dialogues.speaker: Takatoshi
dialogues.text: "You need but stand on this land at midnight, lower your head and recite a special incantation, then your wish will come true!"

response.speaker: Takatoshi
response.text: Looks like you guys really aren't in the loop. This, my friends, is the next big thing. A highly effective wish ritual, guaranteed to make your wishes come true!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A wish ritual? ...That actually works?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This does not sound credible...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right? Even Paimon knows that's just not how the world works.

response.speaker: Takatoshi
response.text: Heh, I didn't believe it at first, either. But that changed when it worked for someone I know.

response.speaker: Takatoshi
response.text: It's this guy called Kunihiko. He's practically always been unemployed, wastes his days away, and he owes a lot of money... like, a lot! But get this — I don't see him for a few days, and suddenly I find him dressed to the nines and feasting at a high-class restaurant!

response.speaker: Takatoshi
response.text: I heard it directly from him. He used this wishing ritual, and the next day he woke up to find his whole bed filled high with Mora!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: His whole bed was filled with M—M—M...!? Woooow!!!

response.speaker: Kiyoto
response.text: Of course, I'm sure the part about waking up lying on a bed of Mora is a bit of an exaggeration.

response.speaker: Kiyoto
response.text: But whether you believe it or not, it's not exactly a difficult ritual. It can't hurt to give it a try, right?

response.speaker: Takatoshi
response.text: If you're still feeling skeptical, just ask around. There are a lot of very compelling stories about this going around these days.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Really? Well c'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's go ask around right now, shall we?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why the sudden urgency?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if it really is true, then just think of all the Mora Paimon could... Oh and you'd finally be reunited with your twin, too! Let's go, let's go!

choices.text: You're so excited you can barely get the words out.

talks.objective: Investigate a kaidan that has been making the rounds recently

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: On closer inspection, it seems like there really are a lot of people talking about this kind of stuff. Hey, see those two? Paimon remembers them from the Yae Publishing House. One's an editor and the other's an author.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: ...Grasp the thought in mind, clear like... ah, clear like the light of the moon. As close as kin with you... no, "thou"... wait, "thee." Uh, hear my... summons, right?

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: No, no, it's not "hear my summons," it's "heed my summons," "heed." *sigh* You're never going to get it down at this rate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what are you guys up to?

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Whoa! Sheesh, you scared me. Okay, okay... Where did I leave off with the incantation, again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Incantation? Are you guys trying out this new wishing ritual stuff, too?

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: Junkichi is trying it out, to be specific. He's hit a bit of a creativity block recently, so I'm helping him make a wish so that he can move past it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I didn't think you guys would believe in this kind of thing.

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: I mean, I obviously don't. But Junkichi never listens to an outside opinion. So all I can do is go along with it.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Mr. Shigeru, can you please be a little more accommodating? This is extremely important to me!

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: People have had all kinds of wishes come true: become more attractive, get rich quick, ace their studies... I'm just a poor, struggling writer looking to get over a creative hurdle. Is that so much to ask?

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Anyway, I just know this is going to work. I have a gut feeling about it.

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: Didn't you say the same thing when you went to make your wish at the Grand Narukami Shrine? "Oh, I just know this is gonna work, I have a gut feeling about it."

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: The omamori from the shrine take too long to have any effect on your luck. Ugh, alright, enough of that, help me get this incantation down. My new book depends on it!

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: *sigh* Look, to be completely honest, I think you need to sit down and have a good think about what kind of story you wanna write. Where's all that self-confidence you had when you first started out?

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: Look at you now! Trying dubious methods from any old light novel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, wait, wait... What? This wishing ritual comes from a light novel?

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Yup. It's from the one called "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it published by Yae Publishing House?

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: No, it's most likely a self-published title. It just appeared out of nowhere and took Inazuma by storm.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: As a fellow writer, I'll refrain from passing comment on how well the story is written. But everyone is saying the wishing incantations it contains are the real deal.

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: Look, Junkichi... yes, everyone's saying it's real, it works, but that's only half the story. I've also heard lots of people saying that everyone who's had their wish granted using this method starts behaving strangely!

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: What's so surprising about that? They're probably just giddy with joy at having their wish come true!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, this is starting to sound a little suspicious...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Why don't we go to the Grand Narukami Shrine and ask Yae Miko about it, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's the expert when it comes to both light novels and the supernatural!

talks.objective: Go to the Grand Narukami Shrine and look for Yae Miko

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miko! Great, you're here.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Well hello there, young ones. What brings you to the shrine? It just so happens that I have a wonderful novel here. I highly recommend it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'd like your expert input on something.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh? Well what did you want to ask?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we were just... Uh, actually, you look kinda busy, is this a bad time?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hehe, no, not at all. It's nothing major.

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: L—Lady Guuji... what do you mean, "nothing major"? I'm begging you, you've gotta help me save my brother!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It really is nothing major, I stand by that. Oh, but since you're so curious, let's have him relate the story one more time, just for you.

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: You two seem to have a good relationship with Guuji Yae. Please, put in a good word for me, you have to convince her to help my brother!

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Here's what happened. My name is Katou Youhei, and my brother is Katou Shingo. All he's ever wanted is to become a swordmaster, so he once asked Sensei Domon of the Meikyou Shisui Art to take him on as a disciple.

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Domon turned him away. Took one look at him and said he didn't have what it takes to train in the art of the sword. But my brother wasn't about to resign himself to defeat — he trained every day as hard as he could, and finally proved himself by defeating one of Domon's best disciples in a duel recently.

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: But since his victory, he's been acting extremely strange. It's like he's become a completely different person... The doctors can't find anything wrong with him, so I'm betting it must be the work of an evil spirit. That's why I'm here begging for Guuji Yae's help...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hahaha... You know, there really aren't as many evil spirits lurking around as you seem to think. Your brother achieved the goal he'd been striving toward for as long as he can remember, and now it's gone. It's only natural that he feels a little empty and lost while he's trying to find a new direction.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: If it were me, I'd just leave him be for a couple of days. He'll recover on his own soon enough.

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: No, Lady Guuji! If you saw him for yourself, you'd know. I guarantee you, he is not acting like someone who feels empty and lost!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, alright, alright. Then tell me, when did your brother spar with Domon's disciple?

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: About... five days ago.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hmm... five days ago, you say...

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Yes, Lady Guuji. That's a long time for him to be acting up like this. I'm really worried about him!

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Our greatest wish is to one day found our own school, just like Domon. We can't jeopardize that dream now!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Wait a minute, now I'm a little confused. Are you here to save your brother, or are you here to make your dreams of founding a martial arts school come true?

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Uh... Well they're kinda two sides of the same coin, aren't they?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hmm? Whatever. Let me ask you this, have you heard of any interesting new rumors lately? If so, I'd love to hear about them.

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Wh—What? Rumors? I... I haven't heard anything!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh dear. Well, that's too bad.

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Lady Guuji, please, stop changing the subject. This is someone's life we're talking about here! Please, you've gotta help me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miko, he seems really desperate. This thing with his brother sounds really bad... Come on, you should help him.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Okay, fine. Then it's decided!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay, Miko! So you're gonna help him?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Katou whatever-your-name-was, these two guests are trusted acquaintances of mine, and in fact they are experts in resolving all manner of strange and supernatural phenomena. Exorcisms and that sort of thing are all in a day's work for them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Uh, wait a sec...

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Um.. r—really!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Is that hesitation that I detect in your voice? So let me get this straight, you come begging to me for help, I actually recommend someone for the job, then suddenly you start doubting me?

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Not at all, never! Whatever Lady Guuji says, I trust wholeheartedly! Thank you two for your willingness to help, please follow me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now hold on a hot second, Miko! We may be a lot of things, but we ain't exorcists!

choices.text: Yeah, this is way beyond our level!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, don't worry. If he wants an exorcism, just grab a handful of salt and mutter some mumbo-jumbo while you're sprinkling it around.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It's a common trope in light novels, right? You just have to have a bit of bravado. As soon as the protagonist gains self-confidence, everything else just magically falls into place.

choices.text: This is not a light novel though...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Well, you were the ones who seemed concerned about his situation. Don't you think it would be a little unfair to make me do all the work?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Besides, we both know you wouldn't be here at the Grand Narukami Shrine unless you had a request for me, too. This is an opportunity to demonstrate that you come in good faith.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... this feels all wrong, but you technically have a point, so...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Alright, let's go. Don't worry, now, I'll be coming along too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Okay, {NICKNAME}, let's follow Youhei and go visit his brother.

choices.text: Pretty sure there's more to an exorcism than "bravado"...
We have no clue about this!

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: Hmm, how strange. My brother's been meditating here pretty much constantly over the past few days, but now he's gone!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Meditating?

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's something that he suddenly started doing after defeating Domon's disciple. He just sits there alone, talking to himself... It's pretty disturbing, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: But that's not important right now! Where the heck could he have gone in his current state?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hmm, this does pose a bit of a problem. If we can't find your brother, well, we can't perform an exorcism with nothing to exorcise, can we?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Katou whatever-your-name-was, given the circumstances, why don't you start by going to find your brother and also picking up a handful of salt on your way. We'll need to use it during the exorcism.

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: Okay... okay, got it! I'm on it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miko, what about us? Shouldn't we help look for his brother, too?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hehe, no need. While what's-his-face is handling that, we'll take a walk around and ask people what they know about the two brothers. Maybe we'll find out some amusing details.

talks.objective: Ask the villagers about Youhei and his brother

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, Sir! We'd like to ask you about the Katou brothers.

dialogues.speaker: Nobuo
dialogues.text: Oh, are you debt collectors? Youhei said to tell you not to worry — he'll be able to pay you back as soon as he has enrolled a few disciples...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Debt collectors? No, no, we're not here for anything like that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, uh, it sounds like Youhei and Shingo have gotten themselves into a bit of a pickle...

dialogues.speaker: Nobuo
dialogues.text: Well, yes, I don't think there's any disputing that. Those two don't have an ounce of dedication between them. They just hop between ideas and won't stick to anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But Youhei said his brother has always wanted to become a swordmaster, and even asked Domon to be his sensei.

dialogues.speaker: Nobuo
dialogues.text: That's true, yes. Shingo begged Domon to take him on and eventually, he finally relented. But even after convincing a renowned sensei to give him a chance, he was the same as ever, bumming around in class instead of focusing on his training.

dialogues.speaker: Nobuo
dialogues.text: In the end, Domon had enough and kicked him out. But Shingo was resentful about it. He blamed Domon for not seeing his potential, and even declared that he would challenge a disciple of Domon to a duel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what? That's not what we heard...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh, how interesting. We heard a slightly different version: "My brother wasn't about to resign himself to defeat — he trained every day as hard as he could, and finally proved himself by defeating one of Domon's best disciples in a duel recently."

dialogues.speaker: Nobuo
dialogues.text: Haha! Youhei said that? That Shingo trained hard? That's ridiculous, he just lay there cussing to high heaven all day, every day. Some training regimen that is.

dialogues.speaker: Nobuo
dialogues.text: Youhei did tell me about Shingo winning the fight, but I took it with a grain of salt. You can ask Kenji at the village entrance more about that. He always has reliable information.

talks.objective: Ask the villagers for more information

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, we've come to ask you about the Katou brothers!

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean Shingo and Youhei?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We heard that Shingo defeated an apprentice of Domon's recently. Is that true?

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: Haha, yes it's true. Wait, so are you here because you heard they're starting their own school and you're looking to sign up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're not here to sign up, but we would like to hear more details about the fight.

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: Well, you've come to the right person. I actually went to watch it.

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: I thought it was a joke when I first heard that Shingo was going to challenge a disciple of the Meikyou Shisui Art. But when he drew his sword, whoa. He became a whole different person.

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: The way he handled his blade, it was like flowing water. Mesmerizing to watch. Domon's disciple is no pushover, but he was absolutely no match for Shingo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is Shingo really that strong!?

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: Yup. He seemed pretty euphoric after winning the duel, too... he was celebrating very vocally, saying something like "What a duel! I haven't felt this good in a long time!"

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hehe, any other details to share? We've heard that Shingo has been behaving rather out of character since then.

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'd definitely say that he has more energy than he used to. In the past, he never used to do much except lie around sunbathing all day.

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: But just yesterday, for example, I saw him cutting down trees for the village head. In the space of one afternoon, he did what most people couldn't finish in three days. Not only that, but he managed to fell a Lavender Melon Tree with just one kick!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hmm... Quite impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: Things got weird after that though. The village head brought out some tofu for him, and he just flipped out. He shouted: "What is that stuff!? Keep that away from me!" then ran off.

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: Lady Guuji. Esteemed exorcists. Finally, I've found you!

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: I found my brother, he's at the waterfall. And I've got the salt you asked for, too. C'mon, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: As much as I'd prefer to stay and hear some more delicious details, I suppose we had better be going now that he's been found.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is Youhei's brother. Whoa, he's meditating while sitting in a waterfall! That's pretty wild!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, listen, he's talking to himself...

dialogues.speaker: Katou Shingo
dialogues.text: Whoo... Hehehe... How's that! Can you... feel it!?

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: Uhhhh...

dialogues.speaker: Katou Shingo
dialogues.text: Can you feel... the feeling... of manliness!

dialogues.speaker: Katou Shingo
dialogues.text: Found your own school... Hah! So shallow... How can a manly man... aspire to something... so... lame!?

dialogues.speaker: Katou Shingo
dialogues.text: ...Ugh... Please, spare me... spare me... I—I can't feel the... m—manliness... I can't even feel the cold anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Katou Shingo
dialogues.text: ...I... I can't take any more... I'm gonna die...

dialogues.speaker: Katou Shingo
dialogues.text: Youhei... Youhei! S—Save me! Save me!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Did you hear that, {NICKNAME}? All the nonsense aside, he's calling for help!

dialogues.speaker: Katou Shingo
dialogues.text: Huh? Who... Who goes there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He stood up... and now he's coming this way!

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: No! Don't come any closer!

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: Help!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What do we do? {NICKNAME}, Miko! Think of something!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Aww, poor thing.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Youhei, your brother's life is hanging in the balance, and he's using his final breaths to call on you for help. Whatever shall we do?

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: Uh, I... Well, how should I know?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The way it looks to me is that Shingo feels terribly resentful to you about something. Would you mind telling me what that's all about?

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: I don't know what to tell you! I don't know!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: You don't know? But surely you should have more insight than anyone else into how your brother came to be this way?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Youhei, I suggest you think very carefully before you open your mouth again. This is a life-or-death situation.

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: Uhhh! Umm... Ummm...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: "Uhhh! Umm... Ummm..."? Your brother is your closest relative. You must have noticed straight away when he started acting out of character.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: And yet five whole days pass before it occurs to you to come and seek help from me. You really expect me not to notice the gaping holes in your story?

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: But I—

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: As you wish. It's fine by me if you don't want to tell the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: But after Shingo dies, you'll be next.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: It's futile trying to escape. Anywhere in the world you run to, it will be right behind your back. After all... you did summon it together.

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: Aaaah!!!!

dialogues.speaker: Katou Youhei
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll talk, I'll talk! I'll tell you everything! ...My brother and I used a wishing incantation. We made a wish!

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Yes! Yes, that's it! The one that's all the rage right now. You just have to recite an incantation at midnight and your wish will be granted!

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Just like the book described, we drew the magic symbol, stepped inside it barefoot at midnight, said the incantation, and lo and behold — spheres of light appeared all around us!

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: After my brother wished to become a swordmaster, it really worked — out of nowhere, he suddenly had these amazing sword skills. But his whole personality changed, too!

choices.text: Why didn't you seek help right away?

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Because... I was worried that if he goes back to normal, he'll lose his skills with the sword.

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: If that happens, it'd ruin our plans to start a martial arts school, and we'd be back to being poor. I just wanted to keep this under wraps until we'd managed to get the dojo set up and paid off our debts...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So then why'd you go to the Grand Narukami Shrine?

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Well, cause with the way he's acting now, I was worried that rumors might start spreading that he's gotten involved in the occult arts or something. And then no one would wanna sign up as his disciple!

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: So I was thinking that maybe Lady Guuji might have a way to get my brother back to normal but let him keep his sword skills...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: My, look at you with your ingenious schemes!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Stop deluding yourself. These new-found sword skills are not his, they belong to the spirit that has possessed him.

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: You're right, you're right! We were wrong to do what we did! We had this coming!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Alright then. Your turn now, my little friend. Toss the salt, and then draw your sword.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What is that!?

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Aaaah!!! It's the s—s—spirit!!!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: See that? That's what you summoned. And look, now that Shingo's no use, it's coming straight for you.

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Waahhh! Save me! Save me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: M—Miko! He fainted! What do we do now?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: We do nothing.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But you, little one. Just a quick fight and this will all be over.

response.speaker: Arakawa Kouji
response.text: Huh... Hahahaha! Who's this? Ah, a fellow swordmaster!

response.speaker: Arakawa Kouji
response.text: Come on! Fight me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #He's coming, {NICKNAME}! Be careful!

choices.text: Why did you wait till now to get him some help?
From "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits"?

talks.objective: Defeat the spirit that has possessed Shingo
Investigate the truth behind the spirit

dialogues.speaker: Arakawa Kouji
dialogues.text: Hehe... Hahaha... That was great, excellent! Wooh! What a rush!

dialogues.speaker: Arakawa Kouji
dialogues.text: I haven't felt this great... in a long, long time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He... disappeared. But he looked pretty content at the end there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh, well, Paimon sure is confused. Do you know what that was all about, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ah, we can talk about it later. They're about to wake up.

response.speaker: Katou Shingo
response.text: *cough cough* ...What am I doing here... Youhei? Youhei, is that you?

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Shingo! Are you alright?

response.speaker: Katou Shingo
response.text: Youhei, I had the weirdest dream...

response.speaker: Katou Shingo
response.text: I dreamed that I wasn't a useless loser with the sword anymore. I even beat one of Domon's disciples.

response.speaker: Katou Shingo
response.text: I thought we could finally open a dojo of our own now... but then I realized, I couldn't control my own body, and there was this voice in my ear talking to me constantly.

response.speaker: Katou Shingo
response.text: I was terrified and I wanted to take control of my body back, but I couldn't. And the voice kept talking about "manliness"...

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Shingo, we shouldn't have made that wish. We summoned a spirit and... it possessed you!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes, and had we not come to your rescue, your life would've been over before too much longer. Then, the spirit would have haunted your brother until he died of fatigue, too.

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Thank you, Lady Guuji! And thank you for your assistance, exorcism experts!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Alright, take him to get some rest. He's very weak right now, having been possessed for quite a few days.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: He will experience a high fever, but it won't be fatal. Remember, this is the price you pay.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: At this point, I would normally lecture you on the dire consequences of using occult methods to obtain power that does not belong to you... but I think you get the picture now, don't you?

response.speaker: Katou Shingo
response.text: Yes... we understand now! We won't ever do it again!

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: Thank you, Lady Guuji! Thank you, exorcists!

response.speaker: Katou Youhei
response.text: We'll be on our way then. Come on, Shingo.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miko, would they really have lost their lives if we hadn't gotten involved?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And if so... why the heck were you so reluctant to help out!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ugh, they would've been fine.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I had to scare them a little, though. Otherwise I hardly think these two lazy rascals would have learned their lesson.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... what was it that possessed Shingo?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You saw it all for yourselves. I'm sure you can figure out what kind of spirit had possessed him, can't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! Paimon's got it! It was an oni!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Correct. Although it possessed Shingo, it didn't have any ill intentions. As a matter of fact, it actually seemed like it was trying to train Shingo to become bolder.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Fair enough, but it seems like it had the opposite effect.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Tossing salt caused it to temporarily leave Shingo's body. Then, you exhausted its strength by fighting it, so it disappeared.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Even if we'd done nothing at all, Shingo would have eventually become too weak for his body to host the spirit, and it would have left of its own accord.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Of course, it would have been more stressful for Shingo and Youhei that way, hehe. Still, the experience may ultimately have been more effective than me scaring them into submission with a little exaggeration.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew... Well, the main thing is that nobody got hurt.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Alright, seems like we've wrapped up everything here. Come on, off we go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on, Miko! You say everything's wrapped up, but are you sure about that?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hmm? You mean you disagree?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, you mean that they got the incantation from that book. Yes, I know the one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, that book's the whole reason we came looking for you at the shrine today. Incantations seem really popular right now.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Human beings don't have powers like us youkai. It's quite understandable for them to be interested in incantations to summon the supernatural.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not the point! The problem is that the incantations in the book are actually capable of summoning spirits and stuff! And loads of people are trying it!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ugh, even then, humans only have so much strength. Even if they do successfully summon a spirit with the incantation, it won't stay with them for very long. I really wouldn't fret about it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But who wrote this book, and why? Don't we think there might be a bigger safety risk here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: It does worry me a bit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Youhei and Shingo may have been fine in the end, but things got pretty scary when Shingo was possessed.

response.speaker: Kuroda
response.text: Lady Yae! I've finally found you.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Kuroda? What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Kuroda
response.text: I'm here to report on Yae Publishing House's sales for the last month. All the numbers are here, please take a look.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Let me see... What? We're losing market share?

response.speaker: Kuroda
response.text: Yes. "Overall Bestseller," "Reader's Favorite," and "Trending Ranking"... We're being beaten in all categories!

response.speaker: Kuroda
response.text: One book is topping all the charts... It's called "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits."

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Both of you, back here, now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miko, what is it? You have a really scary look on your face right now.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Things just got serious. "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" is an all-round hit, summarily beating the novels of the Yae Publishing House by every analysis.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Define "serious"...?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Just what is that supposed to mean!? I worked extremely hard to promote our latest featured work, and now a rival book comes out of nowhere and steals our thunder! If this isn't the very definition of intolerable, I don't know what is.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I have to come up with a counter plan. And you are going to help me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? How is this our problem all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Paimon, please. "Who wrote this book, and why? Don't we think there might be a bigger safety risk here?"

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: *sigh* Am I to take it that the safety of the people of Inazuma isn't so important in your eyes after all?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... what just happened... Again, you technically have a point, but... this feels all wrong!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Nothing's wrong, okay? Come on. We're going to war.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'm going to head back and make some preparations. Meet me outside the Yae Publishing House.

choices.text: If Miko says it's fine, we probably don't need to worry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, when you put it that way... She has been pretty trustworthy so far. She said from the beginning that it wasn't anything major, and so far, there hasn't been any big danger.

choices.text: I'm more curious about Miko's reaction.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right. Big events in the light novel market should be at the center of her attention, surely? But she doesn't seem to care about this book at all.

choices.text: The book, "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits"...

dialogues.speaker: Takatoshi
dialogues.text: Come on, bring me Mora... Mora, Mora, and more Mora...

dialogues.speaker: Kiyoto
dialogues.text: I'm not as greedy as he is... I just wanna get through my exam...

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Grasp the thought in mind, clear like the light of the moon... how does it go after that?

dialogues.speaker: Shigeru
dialogues.text: Junkichi, just give it up. Do you really think someone's going to just descend from the heavens and write your novel for you? I can't believe I'm saying this to a writer, but you need to learn to separate fact from fiction.

dialogues.speaker: Junkichi
dialogues.text: Mr. Shigeru, please! I'd appreciate it if you stopped trying to tear my dreams to smithereens. I am in great distress and desperately need to make a breakthrough!

dialogues.speaker: Nobuo
dialogues.text: I always used to tell Shingo to stop wasting his time, find something worthwhile to do, and stick to it.

dialogues.speaker: Nobuo
dialogues.text: Their parents passed away when they were young, and as the older of the two, he should be setting a good example rather than lazing around all the time... Of course, he wouldn't listen to me.

dialogues.speaker: Nobuo
dialogues.text: In my opinion, he hasn't had things bad enough yet to really feel the heat. He doesn't understand that you have to stay grounded and focused in life.

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: Shingo's been pretty upbeat lately, but for some reason, Youhei's been in a really gloomy mood. I thought they were about to start taking on disciples and start their new chapter — what could be getting him down?

dialogues.speaker: Kenji
dialogues.text: Maybe it's the weight of the responsibility dawning on him? If so, I guess Youhei's finally growing up.
